cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Choose the Relationship
cards.instruction: Make someone prioritize this connection over a competing person, promise, or opportunity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Let work ring. I'd like to finish choosing our wedding vows with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The client won't sign unless I'm there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I'm about to promise you my whole life. Could I have ten minutes before the client?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask Maya to cover. She'll want a reason.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her we're making promises too. Put ours in your calendar beside the client's.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 rank claim and A3 plea for ten minutes do not make superior permission the actual relationship-priority tactic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 requires B for signing, A3 asks only ten minutes first and B4 asks Maya to cover that interval. This need not mean Maya replaces B for signing, so a mandatory factual failure was overstated.

relationship.evidence: B2 business pressure and B4 temporary help offer are plausible competing-duty responses.

heightening.evidence: B4 need for a reason causes A5 to name the couple promises as a calendar-worthy commitment.

specificity.evidence: A1 vows and B2 client establish the conflict; B4 exact cover duties are unspecified but the proposed ten-minute interval provides a coherent scope.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 promises too is earned, while A3 stock reprimand and pleading request remain poorly merged.

coach2.situation: A1 vows and B2 client establish the conflict; B4 exact cover duties are unspecified but the proposed ten-minute interval provides a coherent scope.
coach2.stated: A1 vows unfinished; B2 client needs B; A3 asks ten minutes before client; B4 seeks cover with reason; A5 asks calendar recognition.
coach2.inferred: Temporary cover may hold or manage the client while B finishes, without replacing B signature presence.
coach2.missing: No essential impossibility is established; explicit cover duties would improve clarity but are not a required invented backstory.
coach2.firstDefect: Earlier G2/G3 uncertainty overstated an apparent contradiction by assuming cover meant replacement at signing; that negative judgment is narrowed to the genuine weak Stance.
